narrative:

Your third-year class ranking placed you in the 3rd decile, noticeably lower than the average of roughly 5.8 among accepted students. This weaker academic performance in later law school years was the single biggest reason the model doubted your likelihood of passing the bar. Your LSAT score of 31 also fell short of the 37-point average seen in successful applicants, adding further weight toward a negative outcome. Finally, your undergraduate GPA of 2.7 was below the 3.23 average of those who were admitted, reinforcing the same direction.

Taken together, these academic signals led the model to conclude you were more likely to struggle with the bar exam than to pass it.
